title: StreamYard Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs and Features
summary: StreamYard pricing spans multiple plans, but listed rates don't show the full picture when usage caps and overages factor in. See what you'll actually pay.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


You'll want the answers most likely to change what you pay, so that's what follows. StreamYard's pricing page and help center are the sources, and since both can change, confirm each answer there before you commit.


### The free plan


Is StreamYard free to use? Yes, StreamYard has a free plan, and its pricing page lists what it includes.


Expect the tightest caps and StreamYard's own branding on your streams. That makes it a fair test run, but a poor home for a show you want to look finished.


### Nonprofit and education discounts


Does StreamYard offer a nonprofit or education discount? Don't budget for one unless StreamYard confirms it in writing.


I couldn't verify a standing discount on the pricing page, so ask its support team before you subscribe. If they say yes, get the terms in an email you can find at renewal.


### Cancellations and refunds


Can I cancel StreamYard and get a refund? Treat a payment as final until the billing terms say otherwise.


Cancelling stops the next charge, and the terms of service and help center billing page spell out whether any money comes back. Cancel before the renewal date, not after it.


### Switching plans mid-period


Can I switch plans in the middle of a billing period? Plan changes are made from your account's billing settings, and the help center explains how the charge is handled when you move.


Don't assume a downgrade refunds the unused days. If you can see a busy month coming, upgrade just ahead of it and check what the next invoice will say.


### Extra team members


Does StreamYard charge extra for additional team members? Read the team-member line in each plan's column on the pricing page.


That's where seats are capped, and the cap, not a per-person add-on fee, is what pushes a growing team to the next plan. Count everyone who'll need a login, not only the people who go on screen.
